svg.title: Twelve items, ten scorable, one judge-vs-human confusion matrix
svg.desc: A deterministic mock LLM judge grades 12 labeled items. Its raw verdict is parsed into PASS, FAIL, or ABSTAIN. One refusal is parsed as FAIL and kept in the matrix; one tie and one case of format drift (no VERDICT tag) are parsed as ABSTAIN and dropped, leaving 10 scorable items. On those 10, the judge is scored against human gold with positive class PASS: true positives = 4, false positives = 1, false negatives = 2, true negatives = 3. Human PASS totals 6, human FAIL totals 4; judge-said-PASS totals 5, judge-said-FAIL totals 5; the grand total is 10. From those four counts: accuracy = (4 plus 3) divided by 10 = 0.70, precision = 4 divided by (4 plus 1) = 0.80, recall = 4 divided by (4 plus 2) = 0.67, and F1 = 0.73. The one false positive is a keyword-gamed wrong answer; the two false negatives are correct answers the judge missed for using a synonym or a digit.

svg.text: A judge is just another noisy grader: measure it against humans, on a scorable set, before you trust its score.
